html:
Tucanoan is a family of about two dozen Indigenous languages of the north west Amazon, mostly in the Vaupés basin on the border of Colombia and Brazil, with a western branch in Ecuador, Peru and southern Colombia.

The eastern Tucanoan peoples, among them the Cubeo, the Tatuyo, the Tuyuca, the Siriano and the Yurutí, are known for a rare custom: a person must marry someone who speaks a different language. So most households use two or more languages, and children grow up multilingual. Tukano proper serves as the common language of the region, and even the Arawakan Tariana have largely shifted to it.

The western branch includes the Siona, the Secoya and the Koreguaje. These peoples were hit hard by missions and by the rubber boom of the late 1800s and early 1900s.
sum: Tucanoan is a family of about two dozen Indigenous languages of the north west Amazon, mostly in the Vaupés basin on the border of Colombia and Brazil, with a western branch in Ecuador, Peru and southern Colombia.
